chapter: Brass bands, Eddie Miller and band stories
title: Howard Voorhees and Louis Armstrong's lip
summary: Brownlee recalls Howard Voorhees helping Armstrong with a no-pressure mouthpiece system, and Armstrong's rise from the Waif's Home.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Where was Aunt Lotta from? Was he from New Orleans?
I think he was from New Orleans. I think he was from New Orleans.

I remember people like Howard Vorees, another fine cornet trumpet man, Howard, very fine. In fact, I remember the time Howard saved Louis Armstrong's lip. How was that? With a mouthpiece and with making him play in the center of his mouth. You know, Louis – I remember the days Louis used to run over to the curb when he was playing in the street parade. And rubbed that mouthpiece on the concrete and stick it up in his lip and start blowing. Oh man, he'd really blow it out then, you know. Had that mouthpiece just stuck up in his lip. Well, he was getting to the point where he was about to lose his lip. He was in bad shape. And Howard got him so, man, he could lay that trumpet on the palm of his hand and blow a high C, I mean. I think Howard at that time was promoting a horn that was made there by Couturier. C-O-U-T-E-R-I-E-R, I think it was. They made a very fine trumpet. And they also had a method and a system of mouthpiece and blowing, which they called no pressure system. And Howard got Louis onto that and he practiced on it and practiced on it and he got so that he could… Well, I've seen Howard take a trumpet and hang it by a string and walk up to it and hit high C. No hands, no nothing on it. Just walk up to the instrument hanging by a chord and blow a high C. You can ask Eldon Voorhees, he's there in the Well Line in the Instrument Repair Department. I think he runs that now. I was asking about Howard. He's a very… Of course, it's his brother, but I think he's a very truthful person. Yeah.
I've heard about that. And Louis said it was true.
That was before Louis left town?

No, not necessarily. No, he was back in town. No, Louis had already been up to Chicago and all around. Of course, the Goodwill Ambassador has done very well. Particularly a young boy with nothing. if you want to add it all up from the Waif's home in New Orleans. That could be, as he had been called already, the ambassador of goodwill in the music by playing that horn.
Everybody that knows him likes him.
